watches.name: Amorous Sparta | Automatic | Rectangular watch
watches.description: Sparta is named for the city that built its reputation on restraint. No ornament for its own sake, nothing decorative to hide behind, nothing kept that does not earn its place. That is the same discipline a rectangular case demands, and it is the idea this watch is built around. The Amorous Sparta is a 28 x 40 mm rectangular automatic watch in 800HV hardened stainless steel, 10 mm thick, with a black dial, Roman numerals, a date window at three, and the Swiss Sellita SW100A movement. The case is machined from 800HV hardened steel, a grade roughly twice as scratch resistant as standard 316L stainless, so the polish survives years of daily wear rather than months. At 10 mm it carries the depth an automatic movement needs while still sliding easily under a shirt cuff. The dial is where the restraint shows. Roman numerals sit on an outer ring with a fine minute track, and the centre is finished in a hobnail guilloché that catches the light only when the wrist turns. Black on black, alive from one angle and quiet from another. The date sits at three where it belongs, and the sweeping seconds hand tells you there is a mechanical movement underneath. Sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating keeps the dial clear and glare free in any light. The case back is arched, screwed down and sealed, and 5 ATM water resistance covers rain, showers, swimming and snorkelling. At its core runs the Swiss Sellita SW100A, a 24 jewel automatic beating at 28 800 vibrations per hour with a 42 hour power reserve. It winds itself from the natural motion of your wrist, so there is no battery to replace. Fitted with 20 mm quick release straps and backed by a 10 year warranty. Sparta is not built to be noticed across a room. It is built to be worn every day for a decade and still look like it was made yesterday.

watches.description: The SÖNER Tank Royal Gold is a classic tank watch: a 24 x 34 mm rectangular case in 800HV hardened stainless steel with polished gold plating, 6 mm thick, with a porcelain white dial, Roman numerals, a hidden crown, a Swiss ETA 901.001 quartz movement with an 11-year battery, sapphire crystal and 5 ATM water resistance, backed by a 10-year warranty. "It’s not a copy of the past. It’s an evolution of the form." /Freddie The official launch is scheduled for November and December 2026. Delivery timing makes it an ideal piece for a Christmas present, whether for yourself or a loved one. This is the beginning of a new chapter for SÖNER, the creation of our first ever classic Tank watch, the Söner Tank Royal Gold. A watch born from proportion, angles, and precision. Söner Tank Royal Gold unites 1920s Art Deco elegance, the clean lines of modern Swedish design, and the precision of Swiss heritage. Gold was the metal of the Art Deco era, and on a Tank case it does something steel cannot: it warms the geometry without softening it. Built like a watch. Inspired by a war machine Look closely and you begin to see the details. The baton hands are broad, solid and sharply defined, resembling the silhouette of tank cannons. At exactly 12 o'clock, their alignment creates an especially striking impression: a single barrel pointing toward the top of the dial. Even the numerals carry a unique choice. Almost every watch with Roman numerals, from Cartier to Patek Philippe, Rolex, Longines and most of the other top-tier houses, uses IIII at the 4 o'clock position rather than the grammatically correct IV, a convention chosen for visual balance against the VIII opposite it on the dial. The Söner Tank Royal Gold breaks from that convention and uses the true numeral, IV. It is one of the few watches on the market where the four reads exactly as Roman numerals should. Then there is the case. Its distinctive construction takes inspiration from the caterpillar tracks of a tank. The brancards, the vertical parallel case flanks, are deliberately rounded on the top and flat at the bottom, creating a visual profile reminiscent of the individual sections of a tank track. In gold, those alternating curves and flats catch the light in sequence, so the track pattern reads more clearly than it does in steel. At the heart of the design is a detail you almost don't notice at first: the hidden crown. By concealing the crown within the case architecture, the Söner Tank Royal Gold preserves an unusually clean and symmetrical silhouette. Nothing interrupts the armour-like geometry. From the front, the case becomes a single, disciplined form, much like the uninterrupted surfaces of an armoured vehicle. And finally, the gun turret. The raised upper structures draw inspiration from the gun turret of a tank. They frame the watch from above, giving the case its distinctive vertical architecture and completing the connection between the watch and the machine that inspired it. The Söner Tank Royal Gold draws its character from elegance, engineering and Art Deco. Wear the difference.
